idea.title: One more navigation link exposed a mobile overflow
idea.summary: Adding the Experience link made the footer navigation exceed a 390px mobile viewport. A real browser check identified the footer row as the source, and allowing the links to wrap removed the horizontal overflow.

context.goal: Add an Experience section and keep the portfolio navigation usable on mobile.
context.situation: The portfolio has shared navigation links in both the header and footer, and the section list grew during a job-application content update.
context.problem: At a 390px viewport, the footer's single-line navigation expanded the page to 401px wide.
context.investigation: A Playwright viewport check reported horizontal overflow. Inspecting element bounds showed the footer navigation extending beyond both viewport edges.
context.decision: Keep the existing footer design and let the links wrap on narrow screens rather than reducing the link labels or hiding navigation.
context.implementation: Changed the footer navigation to wrap and use separate horizontal and vertical gaps.
context.result: The mobile page returned to 390px wide with no horizontal overflow; desktop width and mobile menu navigation also passed browser checks.

learning_points: Adding navigation items can break a different shared navigation surface, such as a footer.
Check actual element bounds at a narrow viewport instead of assuming the overflow source.
Wrapping is a small responsive fix that preserves all navigation choices.
story_points: A new section required one additional navigation item.
The footer, not the mobile menu, caused a 11px horizontal overflow at 390px.
A browser check verified the fix without changing the desktop layout.
possible_angles: A navigation change broke the footer on mobile, not the header menu.
How inspecting element bounds made a small responsive regression easy to pinpoint.

resources.description: Small excerpt showing the footer navigation's wrapping and responsive gap classes.
